svg.text: Tier 3: pooled. One multi-tenant app for many clients; Azure enforces each client's data partition on the signed-in user's own token

ADR 0014. For low-sensitivity and standard-content solutions, trials and internal tools. Shared compute, stores and model deployments; per-client containers, indexes, encryption scopes, groups and token limits.
Client users and identity
contoso users (own Entra tenant)
sign in to the multi-tenant app
registration; tid = contoso
adatum users (B2B guests)
guests in Chatham's tenant,
in group sg-aiadv-adatum-users
proseware users
same pattern
App registration: AI Advisory pooled app
(P&T)
app roles Tenant.contoso, Tenant.adatum ...
each client's group is assigned only its
own role; the role arrives in the token
exposes an API scope for on-behalf-of
Entra ID groups (P&T)
sg-aiadv-<tenant>-users per client:
the group IS the data permission
The tenant is never taken from a header,
URL or request body: only from a signed
token claim.
P&T hub (shared)
Azure Firewall
egress allow-list for the pool
routed users -> pool AGW:443
DNS (P&T)
advisor.ai.<domain> -> pool
App Gateway (one host name)
privatelink.* Private DNS
zones
records for the pool's private
endpoints (DINE policy)
Azure Policy
same guardrail initiative
sub: aiadv-pool-eus2-01 (terraform/stamps/pool: one state; tenants are entries in a map)
Every resource here is shared. Per-tenant pieces are sub-resources (containers, indexes, encryption scopes) or role assignments and limits, all created from the tenants map.
vnet-pool01-prd-eus2 (10.120.0.0/22), peered to the hub; 0.0.0.0/0 -> hub firewall
snet-agw
App Gateway WAF_v2 (pool)
one listener: advisor.ai.<domain>
WAF policy + rate limit per client IP
no per-client certificates or listeners
snet-apim
AI gateway (APIM, internal, pool)
validates the signed-in user's token
tenant = Tenant.<code> role claim
token limit + metric per tenant
calls the shared AOAI as its own identity
snet-apps: Container Apps environment (internal)
ca-advisor (pooled, 2+ replicas)
one app, every tenant; resolves the tenant from the
token's Tenant.<code> role, never from input
reads data with the user's token (on-behalf-of), so
Azure checks the user's group on every call
caches keyed by tenant + user; no shared answer cache
job-ingest-<tenant> (one per tenant)
background ingestion has no user, so each tenant's
job runs as its own id-<tenant>-ingest identity
with rights on that tenant's container and index only
pay per execution: near-zero idle cost
snet-pe: private endpoints for the shared storage, search, AOAI and vault
pe-blob
keys off, public off
pe-search
keys off, public off
pe-oai
keys off, public off
pe-kv
keys off, public off
Storage (pool): one container per tenant
RBAC at CONTAINER scope: sg-aiadv-contoso-users and
id-contoso-ingest on container contoso only
encryption scope per tenant (CMK option: revoke the
key to crypto-shred a tenant at offboarding)
Azure AI Search (pool): one index per tenant
RBAC at INDEX scope for the tenant group + ingest id
queries run with the user's token, push only
(indexers would bypass index-level RBAC)
Azure OpenAI (pool): shared deployments
stateless calls only: store=false, no Assistants,
threads, files or stored completions
per-tenant fairness enforced at the gateway
Key Vault (pool)
encryption-scope keys per tenant, TLS cert
Log Analytics (pool)
every row carries the tenant; no prompt bodies;
per-tenant export on request
Per-tenant config (tenants map)
container, index, encryption scope, group and
ingest identity, token limit, monthly token quota
Why a bug in the pooled app can't read another tenant's documents
A contoso user's token carries role Tenant.contoso and group sg-aiadv-contoso-users. The app exchanges it (on-behalf-of) for a storage token and a search token that are still
that user's.
Storage holds a role assignment for sg-aiadv-contoso-users on container 'contoso' only; Search on index 'contoso' only. If the code asks for container 'adatum', Azure returns
The app's own managed identity has NO data role on storage or search. It only pulls images and writes telemetry. Model calls carry the user's token to the gateway, which keys
token limits on Tenant.<code>.
What is weaker than Tiers 1 and 2 (say it first)
One process serves every tenant: a memory or cache bug could mix answers. Mitigated by tenant + user
cache keys and no semantic cache, not eliminated. One Azure OpenAI quota and one outage domain for
all tenants; gateway limits keep it fair. No per-tenant network path or CMK on logs. A regulator or
client who asks 'is anything of ours processed alongside other clients?' gets a yes.
What it costs (approx. list price, USD/month)
Shared per pool: App Gateway ~400, APIM ~700 (Standard v2*), Search S1 x2 ~490, app replicas ~120,
Log Analytics ~80, Azure OpenAI pay per token. About 1,800 per pool.
Per tenant: a container, an index, an encryption scope, a group, a job identity: ~5 + tokens.
At 45 tenants (the cap, under S1's 50 indexes): ~45 per tenant. Onboarding: same day.
*Premium APIM (internal VNet mode, as built today) is ~2,800: ~90 per tenant at 45.
Fits / doesn't fit
Fits: internal Chatham tools, standard-content products (market commentary, rate and hedge
explainers over Chatham's own research), trials and proofs of concept, small clients whose
data classification is internal or public and whose contract allows logical isolation.
Doesn't fit: confidential client documents, client-specific models or fine-tunes, PTU, CMK
requirements on everything, or a client-owned network path. Those go to Tier 2 or Tier 1.
Legend
Owned by Platform Engineering (P&T)
Shared by every tenant in the pool
Per tenant (partition, identity or limit)
Users
Key isolation control
User path: one host name -> pool App Gateway -> pooled app (tenant from the token)
Data path on the user's own token: Azure checks container- and index-scoped roles
Model path: user's token -> AI gateway (per-tenant limits) -> shared Azure OpenAI
Ingestion: per-tenant job identity -> that tenant's container and index only
Egress: pool workload subnets -> hub firewall (UDR)
Sources: docs/adr/0014-isolation-tiers.md, docs/architecture/isolation-tiers.md, terraform/stamps/pool. Names are the example config.
